title: Projection and lag alignment changes sign after global signal removal in 13 larval zebrafish
abstract: We tested whether regional projection direction predicts slow calcium lead and lag patterns in 13 larval zebrafish. We linked public imaging and a mapZebrain projectome across 60 regions and 1,770 pairs. At one-volume lag, the mean orientation correlation was -0.155 before adjustment. After removal of additive region timing patterns, the primary mean was -0.016 (fish bootstrap 95% interval -0.031 to -0.002; two-sided exact sign-flip p=0.071). The primary test did not support positive alignment. Removing the global signal gave a small positive adjusted mean of 0.041 (0.017 to 0.065). Residual lag patterns agreed across recording halves (mean 0.417) and across fish. Symmetric structure predicted simultaneous correlation (mean r=0.422). Thus, a simultaneous structure-function relation and stable lag patterns did not yield a processing-stable projection-lag relation. The projection matrix uses neurite terminals from other animals, and the imaging rate is about one volume per second. These data do not identify synaptic causality or fast transmission. Code, exact input hashes, aggregate results, and numerical checks are supplied.

display.caption: Projection and lag orientation changes with region timing controls and global signal removal. Each line is one fish. Error bars are fish bootstrap 95% intervals. Residual lag patterns remain stable across recording halves.
